results.summary: This design generates a VGA signal displaying moving coloured concentric circles. It uses a standard hvsync generator and outputs 2-bit per channel colour signals. It requires an external Tiny VGA PMOD and a VGA monitor to view the output. The design is a basic demo intended for testing VGA output on Tiny Tapeout.

ASAP CPU v2 is an 8-bit SAP-1 style computer inspired by Ben Eater's breadboard CPU. It includes a program counter, RAM, registers, ALU, and a control unit, and can be programmed via switches. It outputs results to a multiplexed 7-segment display and requires external switches and displays for operation. The design is intended for educational purposes and includes a cocotb testbench.

This project implements a streaming byte-fed sequential and combinational accumulator generated from MLIR for-loop patterns. It detects specific loop shapes and emits a specialized S3FDP accumulator instead of generic floating-point logic. The design has 8-bit input and output ports and requires no external hardware. It demonstrates a compiler flow using Emeraude and CIRCT to optimize arithmetic operations.

Project Long Man is a quasi-delay-insensitive die-to-die interconnect that streams data via SPI. It uses toggle-based encoding on TX/RX lines to reduce switching activity. The design can be tested by tying RX and TX together and controlling it through SPI signals. No external hardware is required.

PicoMIPS CPU is a basic MIPS-like processor with a 24-bit program word, 4-bit code memory, and a 16x8-bit register file. It includes a clock prescaler and a shift register for instruction loading. The CPU can be halted and interrupted, and it outputs address and status signals. It requires an oscilloscope for testing the prescaler and is based on an old university project.

This design is an 8-bit processor with 16-bit instructions that interacts with VGA output. It fetches programs from external QSPI flash and uses external RAM, outputting VGA signals. It requires a QSPI PMOD for flash and RAM and a TinyVGA PMOD for video output. The processor starts executing from address 0 after reset.

Luz generates a VGA signal, likely displaying some visual pattern. It requires a Tiny VGA PMOD and a monitor, and is clocked at 80 MHz. The documentation is minimal, providing only a brief description and testing steps. No further details about the visual output are given.

The SIMD2 Math Accelerator Unit is a 4-bit ALU pipeline that performs various vector and scalar math operations. It communicates over an SPI-style interface using a 20-bit instruction word. The design supports operations like dot product, vector add/sub, and distance squared. It is intended as a hardware accelerator for math-intensive tasks.

This project implements five analog comparators using only digital standard cells from SKY130. The comparators take analog inputs and produce digital outputs, with some requiring an external clock. Testing requires a signal generator and oscilloscope to observe the comparator behavior. It demonstrates analog functionality using digital cell libraries.

Tiny PI Controller implements a simple PI controller with a UART interface for configuration and data exchange. It is designed for control systems applications like motor control, where the derivative term is not needed. The controller can receive sensor values and output computed PI values over UART, with configurable Kp, Ki, and setpoint. It requires an external 12 MHz clock and a UART-capable device.
